findings.where: Hero, the 'Write to Mark' button and the amber-hatched third bay of the section drawing above it (desktop-01, phone-01); the palette names amber as both 'daylight in the drawing, and the one action'
findings.fault: The primary action's colour is also used on decoration. Sodium amber fills the button, and it also marks the brightest spot in the drawing, the hatched bay, which sits above the button and catches the eye first. Amber is supposed to mean 'act here', but on the first screen it also means 'daylight'. The bay is the first amber a visitor sees and it does nothing, so the colour stops pointing only at the button.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development bank scanning the first screen for how to contact Mark. Their eye goes to the amber bay before the button and finds it doesn't respond. Mark would object too: the one call to action is meant to be the only thing on the sheet asking to be pressed.

findings.where: Title block / nav bar: the 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS' cells next to the PROFILE, ARTICLES, BLOG and CONTACT cells (desktop-01 top row; phone-01, where they sit beside the logo above the nav row)
findings.fault: The nav links and the static drawing-number and scale cells look the same: equal ruled cells in one row, light text on blue. Position is the only thing that shows a nav item is a link, and here clickable and non-clickable cells share the row. 'MMM-GA-001' and 'NTS' look like two more menu items, but clicking them does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor looking for their way around the site. They can't tell from the bar which cells are links, and may click 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page such as a project or document.

findings.where: Hero, 'Write to Mark' (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com); the address is never shown on the page
findings.fault: The page's one action is only a mailto link, and the email address itself appears nowhere on the page. Clicking it on a machine with no mail app set up opens nothing, or opens the wrong app. The visitor then has no address to copy into their own webmail.
findings.who_objects: Staff at multilateral banks and agencies, who often work in locked-down webmail or on managed machines where mailto does nothing. For them the primary action fails, with no workaround visible.

findings.where: Article specimen, the related-item box 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge — Lecture · 2026-04-23 · PDF' (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The item sits in its own bordered box, which reads as one card you can tap anywhere. Only the underlined title is a link, so taps on the box, the 'Lecture · date · PDF' line or the empty space do nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader on a phone who taps the card's meta line or the space around it to open the lecture PDF, and nothing happens. Angélique will add many of these items, so the mismatch repeats across the site.

findings.fault: A button that acts in place is styled as an underlined text link, which is the look the page keeps for navigation (the article link above it is underlined the same way). It looks as if it will take you somewhere, when it actually replays the animation where it is.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined label to open a page and hesitates before clicking. The layout round would also inherit two meanings for the same underline.
